To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sheaf quotient of an affine superscheme over a finite supergroup is again an affine scheme and the algebra of functions of this quotient is a finitly presented progenerator as an algebra over the algebra of functions on the quotient of this affine superscheme.

the sheaf quotient of an affine super scheme X over a field of characteristic different from 2 with respect to fppfs is again an affine super scheme Y, where K[X] ≃ K[Y] and K[X] is finitely presented as a K[X]-module, provided that a finite supergroup acts freely on X.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding a geometric interpretation of the quotient ring K[X]G in the case when X and G are affine superschemes over K, and the action of G on X is free.
the following question: when is the sheaf quotient of two affine super schemes X and Y with respect to the action of a finite group G an affine super scheme?
the problem of finding an explicit presentation of the sheaf quotient of X/G in terms of the coordinate ring of X.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

if G is a finite supergroup acting on an affine superscheme then the corresponding sheaf quotient exists, is an affine superscheme, and the ring of functions is finitely presented over the ring of functions on the quotient.
the category of affine superschemes X over a finite supergroup is equivalent to the category of affine K-algebras A, which are finitely presented as progenerators as K[X]G-modules.
the quotient of an affine superscheme by an action of a free finite supergroup is an affine supergroup.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we prove the existence of the sheaf quotient in the case of finite supergroups.
we have given an algebraic version of the well known result in topology: if G acts freely, then the quotient space is again a manifold.
we give a description of the quotient of affine superschemes over finite superschemes in terms of the corresponding rings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can define a quotient X/G of an affine super scheme by a finite super group G, which is a super scheme, such that K[X/G] = K[X]G, and that K[X] is finitely presented as a module over K[X]G.
the sheaf quotient of an affine superscheme over a finite supergroup is again an affine super scheme.
we have found a way to generalize a theorem of Grothendieck to supergroups.
